reasoning_trace.description: The paper proposes a direct-current-biased optical OFDM (DCO-OFDM) scheme for free space optical (FSO) integrated sensing and communication (ISAC). The system model is illustrated in Fig. 1, which shows the FSO-ISAC transceiver based on a LiDAR. The signal processing procedures are described, including the time-domain OFDM signal expression and the clipping noise modelled by the Bussgang theorem.
reasoning_trace.value: The system model of the DCO-OFDM scheme for FSO-ISAC is illustrated in Fig. 1, which shows the FSO-ISAC transceiver based on a LiDAR.

reasoning_trace.description: The paper formulates an optimization problem in the communication-centric scenario, which jointly optimizes the direct-current (DC) bias and the normalized power allocation for each subcarrier. The non-convex optimization problem is decomposed into two sub-problems to obtain a concise solution, and an iterative algorithm is proposed to optimize power allocation.
reasoning_trace.value: The optimization problem is formulated to maximize the spectral efficiency for communication while guaranteeing the sensing precision.

reasoning_trace.description: The paper conducts numerical simulations to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm and reveal the trade-off between communication and sensing functionalities of the OFDM-based FSO-ISAC. reasoning_trace.value: The numerical simulations demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm and reveal the trade-off between communication and sensing functionalities.
